To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the tropism of HIV-2 can be predicted by using genotypic tropin test based on provirial DNA in HIV-2 infected patients with low or unetectable viral load, which is a useful tool for tropism determinaton.
HIV-2 genotyping of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) is a reliable tool for HIV-2 tropic strain determination, especially in patients with undetectable or low viral load.
HIV-2 genotyping based on proviral HIV-2 DNA is a suitable method for HIV-2 tropisms determination in HIV-1-infected patients with undetectable viral plasma HIV-2 RNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new method for the prediction of HIV-1 tropism, which is based on the analysis of the V3 region of gp120, the main determinant of the coreceptor usage, by a novel algorithm, the so called “V3-GenoScore”.
the use of the HIV-2 tropic test in the context of HIV-2 treatment and its clinical implications.
a novel method of determining the coreceptor tropism of HIV-2, which is a promising tool in the management of patients with advanced HIV-2 infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIV-2 genotyping tropism assay based on proviral genomic DNA is a suitable and valid tool for the tropism determination in the HIV-2-infested patients with low or even undetectable viral loads.
HIV-2 tropic phenotype is not associated with disease progression in HIV-2 infection.

HIV-1 tropism testing should be performed in all patients starting cART with a detectable viral load, and in all patients with a viral load below the limit of detection who are starting cART for the first time or are switching to a new cART regimen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concordance of HIV-2 genotyping based on plasma RNA or proviral DNA is high, but it is not perfect.
, in HIV-2, genotypic tropismprediction from proviral DNA is more accurate than that from RNA.
the HIV-2 tropic test based on provirus is a suitable tool in HIV-2 patients with low or non-detectable viral load in plasma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tropism prediction based on proviral HIV-2 DNA is more accurate in the context of low viral load.
, in HIV-2, the concordances between plasma RNA and PBMC DNA genotypic tropisms are not high enough to warrant the use of plasma RNA tropism tests.
HIV-2 genotyping tropism tests based on proviral or circulating RNA can be used interchangeably, and the use of plasma RNA is not mandatory.
